chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Abdillah al-Razi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from his father, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the cow and other animals that are given water or fed with what is not permissible for a Muslim to eat or drink. Is that disliked? He said, 'Yes, that is disliked.'
ai.seo_question: Is it disliked to feed cows non-halal food?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while feeding livestock with non-halal substances is not strictly prohibited (haram), it is considered disliked (makruh). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between absolute prohibition and recommended avoidance, emphasizing the purity of the animal's body and milk for human consumption. It reflects the broader principle that the permissibility of an animal's produce depends on its diet, provided the impurity does not render the animal itself unlawful to slaughter.
